candidates.hypothesis: When two or more already-fixed candidate sources compete for one cash-feasible slot, choosing the highest standalone candidate score can overpay for correlated exposure and execution impact; a frozen net-replacement allocator that subtracts only predeclared incremental exposure and liquidity-cost penalties may improve portfolio-level replacement value without creating a new signal.
candidates.why_not_arbitraged: Standalone candidate scores are produced on different source clocks and do not price the marginal correlation, crowding, spread, or participation cost of the exact slot they displace; any edge must come from that pre-decision portfolio externality, not from refitting the underlying signals.
candidates.falsifier: The mechanism is falsified if it changes fewer than five actual same-slot choices in any canonical window, cannot bind point-in-time exposure and cost fields, or fails to improve net replacement value while preserving drawdown and concentration relative to the current cash-feasible one-slot allocator.

baseline.policy: Use the current one-slot cash-feasible allocator and its existing candidate ordering without a portfolio-correlation or impact penalty.
baseline.universe: already-fixed eligible candidates competing for the same cash-feasible slot

treatment.policy: Within an actual same-slot conflict only, choose the candidate with the highest frozen standalone score minus predeclared incremental exposure-correlation, spread, and participation-impact penalties; preserve every source's entry, exit, horizon, notional cap, and eligibility rule.

candidates.replacement_value_comparator: The exact candidate or cash displaced by the current cash-feasible one-slot allocator, plus SPY and QQQ context under identical capital and cost constraints.

execution_envelope.borrow_dependency: none; this allocator cannot create short positions
execution_envelope.capacity_constraint: one existing cash-feasible slot with unchanged per-source notional caps
execution_envelope.costs_and_carry: canonical cash-equity costs plus one frozen nonlinear-impact stress function
execution_envelope.intended_instrument: the original liquid cash equity emitted by each fixed source
execution_envelope.liquidity_dependency: point-in-time spread, ADV, and planned participation rate must be available for every changed choice
execution_envelope.timing_constraint: all exposure and cost features must be known before the same decision clock as the baseline allocator

candidates.title: Cost- and correlation-adjusted one-slot replacement allocator

prediction.confidence_reason: The economic mechanism is distinct from trend selection, but the portfolio exposure and nonlinear-cost surfaces are not yet bound to historical decisions, allocator conflicts remain under the registered reopen count, and nearby covariance/allocator overlays are frozen.

candidates.reopen_condition: Bind sanitized point-in-time exposure and spread/impact fields to at least 20 settled same-slot conflict decisions, while proving that the proposed allocator is a genuinely different decision mechanism rather than a covariance-weight or source-priority retune.
candidates.next_machine_action: Run opposite-runtime challenge and outcome-blind D0-D3 only; do not reserve an experiment unless the source binding and history veto both pass.
